title: Telangana CM Sacks Minister Konda Surekha From Cabinet Over Party Indiscipline
excerpt: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy removed the Forest and Environment minister after Congress high command backed disciplinary action triggered by her daughter's public attacks on party leadership.
body:
• Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy removed Konda Surekha from the state cabinet on Thursday, September 3, following a Congress high command directive over indiscipline.
  • The crisis began when Surekha's daughter, Konda Sushmitha Patel, publicly attacked the CM and announced her intention to contest from the Parkal constituency without party authorisation.
  • More than 20 Congress MLAs and MLCs demanded action against Surekha; Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge ruled that public criticism of party leadership breached discipline.
  • The government also rescinded G. Chinna Reddy's appointment as Planning Board vice-chairman and made several new administrative appointments.

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Thursday removed Forest, Environment and Endowment Minister Konda Surekha from his Council of Ministers with immediate effect. The recommendation for her removal has been formally sent to Governor Jishnu Dev Varma.

How the Crisis Unfolded

The internal Congress dispute erupted in August when Surekha's daughter, Konda Sushmitha Patel, delivered sharp public remarks against Revanth Reddy at an event in Parkal constituency. She accused the chief minister of favouring family members in business dealings and declared her intention to contest the next assembly election from Parkal — a seat currently held by Congress MLA Revuri Prakash Reddy, whom the CM had publicly backed for renomination.

The statements triggered a firestorm within the Telangana Congress. More than 20 party MLAs and MLCs, along with several cabinet ministers, formally demanded stringent action against both Surekha and her daughter.

High Command Steps In

The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) disciplinary committee issued a notice to Surekha and initiated inquiries. Surekha maintained throughout that her daughter's remarks were personal opinions and that she should not be held responsible for them.

She travelled first to Bengaluru and then to Delhi to meet Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge. In those meetings, Kharge made clear that public criticism of the chief minister and unilateral declarations about candidacies breached party discipline, noting that candidate selections are the exclusive domain of the central leadership.

"Expecting another person to take political responsibility or demanding an explanation for someone's opinions merely due to family relations is improper."

— Konda Surekha, in her submission to the TPCC disciplinary committee

Surekha refused to resign and asserted that any action against her should also apply to the chief minister. The final decision came Thursday after Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal met Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, capping three days of consultations involving Revanth Reddy, Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka and state president Mahesh Kumar Goud.

Administrative Reshuffle

Alongside Surekha's removal, the state government rescinded the appointment of senior Congress leader G. Chinna Reddy as vice-chairman of the Telangana Planning Board following his comments against Wanaparthy MLA T. Megha Reddy.

The CM made three new appointments: Gadwal Vijayalakshmi as vice-chairperson of the Planning Board, Nerella Sharada as chairperson of the Telangana State Commission for Women, and former Rajya Sabha member G. Sudha Rani as chairperson of the Kakatiya Urban Development Authority (KUDA).

Surekha's Political Journey

Konda Surekha has a long and turbulent political history in Telangana. She has switched between Congress and TRS (now BRS) multiple times, most recently rejoining Congress in 2018. She was allocated the Forest, Environment and Endowments portfolio when Revanth Reddy formed his cabinet in December 2023 after Congress swept the Telangana assembly elections.

In 2024, she courted controversy with remarks about actor Naga Chaitanya's divorce from Samantha Ruth Prabhu, which led to a defamation lawsuit. Her latest removal marks another dramatic chapter in a political career defined by confrontation.

What Comes Next

The removal takes formal effect once Governor Jishnu Dev Varma acts on the recommendation. The episode has laid bare factional tensions within Telangana Congress that extend well beyond the immediate dispute over Sushmitha's remarks. Whether the party can contain the fallout — particularly among backward-class leaders who view Surekha's ouster as targeted — will shape the internal dynamics ahead of the next state election cycle.
